⚡️🤖 The AI race is becoming an energy race

China is currently building 39 nuclear reactors—more than the next 12 countries combined. Meanwhile, the U.S. has zero large commercial nuclear reactors under construction.

The massive expansion is widely seen as part of China's strategy to secure enough electricity for the next generation of AI infrastructure. But there's another critical bottleneck: power transformers.

As AI data centers consume ever more energy, the industry is discovering that the biggest shortage isn't chips—it's electrical infrastructure. Transformers are expensive, built to order, difficult to automate, and production lead times now stretch for years. Around 40% of new U.S. data centers are already facing delays due to power constraints.

In the AI era, electricity may become just as valuable as computing power. ⚛️⚡️

The count of rounds nearly tripled over the same period: 12 → 33 per quarter, and now holds steady over 30 for three consecutive quarters.

Crypto funding is consolidating into fewer, larger deals: the long tail of smaller rounds keeps thinning out, while capital concentrates at the top of the market. For the crypto market, this means that the market matures as grown projects receive more attention from VCs.

📌 Rehypothecation: When One Collateral Base Works Twice

Main Points
⏺ In DeFi, the same collateral can indirectly back multiple obligations
⏺ It boosts capital efficiency but increases systemic fragility
⏺ This post explains how “leverage on top of leverage” forms

1️⃣ How It Happens — you post collateral, borrow against it, then reuse the borrowed asset as collateral elsewhere.
2️⃣ Why People Do It — yield strategies and capital efficiency: more output from the same base.
3️⃣ Where Risk Lives — a price drop can trigger cascading liquidations across layers.
4️⃣ Why It Matters — calm markets hide the links; stress markets push correlations toward 1.
5️⃣ Practical Rule — count how many collateral layers your strategy has and model a sharp drawdown.

Final Thoughts

Rehypothecation is an accelerator. It adds efficiency, but it makes systems brittle when markets break.

FERMENTED TURMERIC RECIPE

INGREDIENTS  
1.5 cups turmeric roots, peeled and grated  
2 tsp sea salt  
1 cup filtered water  
1 tbsp kefir (starter culture)

PREPARATION  
Place the grated turmeric into a pint-sized wide-mouth mason jar.  
Add the water and salt to create a brine, leaving about 2 inches of space at the top.  
Mix in the starter culture.  
Seal the jar with a glass weight (like a pickle pebble) and an airlock lid.  
Let it ferment for 4–5 days.  
After fermentation, store in the refrigerator — it will keep for up to a year.

NOTE:  
If you're fermenting during October in a sunny climate, the natural sunlight may be strong enough to kickstart fermentation — in that case, a starter culture isn’t necessary.
